parsed.title: Geometric bounds conjecture for spanning trees of finite planar graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite connected planar graph, let $\tau(\Gamma)$ be its number of spanning trees, and let ${\rm vol}(\Gamma)={\rm vol}(S^3-K)$ for the alternating link $K$ associated to $\Gamma$. **Geometric bounds conjecture.** If ${\rm vol}(\Gamma)>0$, then

$$
{\rm vol}(\Gamma)<2\pi\log\tau(\Gamma)<|E\Gamma|v_{\rm oct}.
$$

This finite-graph analogue relates hyperbolic volume and spanning-tree complexity. It is presented as a conjectural extension of known geometric inequalities for alternating links; its general status is open.
parsed.source_name: Abhijit Champanerkar and Ilya Kofman, “Geometric bounds for spanning tree entropy of planar lattice graphs”, arXiv:2505.05688 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05688

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: Grünbaum's toroidal conjecture on non-3-edge-colorable cubic graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a $2$-connected cubic graph embedded in the torus. **Grünbaum's conjecture.** If $G$ is not $3$-edge-colorable, then $G$ contains two edges on the same face of the embedding whose removal gives a planar graph in which the four endpoints of the removed edges lie on the boundaries of two faces. The conjecture is false in general for surfaces of genus $5$, as shown by Kochol, but the paper proves the toroidal case.
parsed.source_name: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar and Tomohiro Sonobe, “Three-edge-coloring (Tait coloring) cubic graphs on the torus: A proof of Grünbaum's conjecture”, arXiv:2505.07002 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07002

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2025). “Today, it is known that the general conjecture does not hold for the surface of genus 5, as proved by Kochol .”

parsed.title: The degeneracy-graph connectivity conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, and let $DG(2n)$ be the degeneracy graph. **The degeneracy-graph connectivity conjecture.**
1. The graph $DG(2n)$ is connected when regarded as an undirected graph.
2. Every vertex with no incoming arrows has dimension $n$ and is of the form $l_C$ for some $C\in\mathrm{UConf}(2n)$.

The paper records basic dimension and arrow properties and expects these two global properties of the degeneracy graphs.
parsed.source_name: Andrei Grigorev and Evgeny Mukhin, “On representations of quantum affine sl_2”, arXiv:2505.11605 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11605

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: The conf-connected deletion conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $w=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{2n})$ be a conf-connected word, let $a$ be its minimal letter, and let $I_w(a)$ denote the positions occupied by $a$. Set

$$
i=\max(I_w(a)),\qquad j=\max(I_w(a+2)).
$$

Let $\mathring{w}_{\{(i,j)\}}$ be the word obtained by deleting the letters in positions $i$ and $j$. **The conf-connected deletion conjecture.** The word $\mathring{w}_{\{(i,j)\}}$ is conf-connected.

The statement is proposed as a combinatorial route toward the degeneracy-graph connectivity conjecture. The paper does not provide a proof or resolution.
parsed.source_name: Andrei Grigorev and Evgeny Mukhin, “On representations of quantum affine sl_2”, arXiv:2505.11605 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11605

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: The bounded tree-independence conjecture for $\{P_k,K_{t,t}\}$-free graphs
parsed.statement:
For positive integers $k$ and $t$, let a graph be **$\{P_k,K_{t,t}\}$-free** if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to the $k$-vertex path $P_k$ or to $K_{t,t}$.

**Bounded tree-independence conjecture.** For any two positive integers $k$ and $t$, the class of $\{P_k,K_{t,t}\}$-free graphs has bounded tree-independence number.

The conjecture is open already in this special case, as stated in the source.
parsed.source_name: Claire Hilaire, Martin Milanič and Đorđe Vasić, “Treewidth versus clique number. V. Further connections with tree-independence number”, arXiv:2505.12866 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12866

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2025). “Chudnovsky and Trotignon (see ).”

parsed.title: Burness–Giudici Common Neighbour Conjecture for Saxl graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G\leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a primitive permutation group with base size $b(G)=2$, and let $\Sigma(G)$ be its Saxl graph, whose vertices are the points of $\Omega$ and whose edges are the 2-element bases of $G$. **Common Neighbour Conjecture.** Any two vertices of $\Sigma(G)$ share a common neighbour. Consequently, $\operatorname{diam}(\Sigma(G))\leq 2$. This conjecture concerns the connectedness and diameter of Saxl graphs associated with primitive groups of base size two; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.
parsed.source_name: Melissa Lee and Anthony Pisani, “The Saxl hypergraph of a permutation group”, arXiv:2505.13849 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13849

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: Covering graph conjecture for 2-token graphs of stars
parsed.statement:
Let $K_{1,n}$ be the star graph with $n$ leaves. Suppose that $n$ divides $\binom{n+1}{2}$. A **combined voltage assignment** $(\alpha,\omega)$ on a base graph $X$ with values in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ defines a covering graph $X^{(\alpha,\omega)}$.

**Covering conjecture for 2-token star graphs.** The token graph $F_2(K_{1,n})$ is isomorphic to a covering graph $X^{(\alpha,\omega)}$ of a base graph $X$ on $n-k$ vertices, with combined assignment on the group $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$.

The conjecture summarizes the preceding examples and discussion for 2-token graphs of stars; no resolution is supplied in the source.
parsed.source_name: Sergio G. Gómez-Galicia and Octavio B. Zapata-Fonseca, “Edge-transitive token graphs as covers”, arXiv:2505.20632 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20632

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: Spectral Turán conjecture for non-bipartite books
parsed.statement:
Let $B_{r+1}$ denote the graph consisting of $r+1$ triangles sharing a common edge, and let $\rho(G)$ be the spectral radius of a graph $G$. A graph is **$B_{r+1}$-free** if it contains no copy of $B_{r+1}$. Let $S_{m,1}^{+}$ be the graph obtained from $K_{1,m-1}$ by adding an edge within its independent set. **Non-bipartite book conjecture.** If $G$ is a non-bipartite $B_{r+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges, then

$$
\rho(G)\leq\rho\big(S_{m,1}^{+}\big),
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong S_{m,1}^{+}$. This conjecture concerns the spectral extremal graph among non-bipartite book-free graphs; the source proposes it without giving a resolution.
parsed.source_name: Ruifang Liu and Lu Miao, “Spectral Turán problem of non-bipartite graphs: Forbidden books”, arXiv:2506.04884 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04884

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The distinguishing proper arc-colouring conjecture for complete symmetric digraphs
parsed.statement:
Let $\overleftrightarrow{K_n}$ be the complete symmetric digraph on $n$ vertices. Write $\chi'_{D_{2}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_n})$ for its distinguishing proper arc-colouring number, and let $\chi'_{2}(\overleftrightarrow{K_m})$ denote the corresponding proper arc-colouring number under the paper's type-II condition. **The distinguishing proper arc-colouring conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_{D_{2}}(\overleftrightarrow{K_{n}}) = \chi'_{2}(\overleftrightarrow{K_{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil}})+1.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the distinguishing number for complete symmetric digraphs is obtained from the type-II parameter at half the order, with one additional colour. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
parsed.source_name: Rafał Kalinowski, Monika Pilśniak and Magdalena Prorok, “Distinguishing symmetric digraphs by proper arc-colourings of type I”, arXiv:2506.13979 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13979

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The quasi-isomorphism refinement of the Orlik–Solomon conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a geometric lattice. Let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{L})$ be its Orlik–Solomon algebra, and let $\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{L}}$ be the map defined in the source. **Quasi-isomorphism refinement.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $\mathcal{L}$ is supersolvable.
2. $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{L})$ is Koszul.
3. $\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

This is proposed as a refinement of the classical Orlik–Solomon Koszulness conjecture. The source does not give a resolution, so the refinement remains open.
parsed.source_name: Basile Coron, “Matroid complexes and Orlik-Solomon algebras”, arXiv:2506.15048 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15048

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The maximal-independent-set conjecture for graphs with perfect matchings
parsed.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph on $n$ vertices containing a perfect matching. A **maximal independent set** is an independent vertex set that is not properly contained in any larger independent set. **The perfect-matching maximal-independent-set conjecture.** $
\Gamma$ contains at most

$$
2^{n/2}
$$

maximal independent sets.
This is posed as a conjecture about extremal enumeration in graphs with perfect matchings; the source gives no resolution, so the asserted bound remains open.
parsed.source_name: Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, “Notes on sum-free sets in abelian groups”, arXiv:2506.17401 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The planar-duality-after-vertex-deletion conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be cyclically $6$-connected $4$-regular graphs. Suppose there are vertices $v_i\in V(G_i)$ such that $G_i\setminus\{v_i\}$ are planar and dual to each other.

**Planar deletion-duality conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathsf{N}_2(G_1)=\mathsf{N}_2(G_2).
$$

This is a special case of the period--Speyer conjecture and concerns graphs that need not themselves be planar. The paper gives it as an implication of the broader conjecture, with examples motivating the relation.
parsed.source_name: Erik Panzer, “Graph theoretic properties of Speyer's matroid polynomial g_M(t)”, arXiv:2506.18788 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18788

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The Martin-sequence determination conjecture for Speyer's invariant
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a cyclically $6$-connected $4$-regular graph or a cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graph. Let $G^\bullet$ denote the associated vertex-deleted or suitably marked graph, and let $\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^\bullet)$ be its Martin sequence.

**Martin-sequence conjecture.** The Martin sequence $\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G^\bullet)$ determines the value of $\mathsf{N}_2(G)$.

This proposes that the Martin invariant data contain enough information to recover Speyer's second invariant on these highly connected graph classes. The paper states it as an expectation and provides no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Erik Panzer, “Graph theoretic properties of Speyer's matroid polynomial g_M(t)”, arXiv:2506.18788 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18788

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The stabilizer conjecture for the sets $W_l'$ in three-reflection presentations
parsed.statement:
Let $D_n$ be a dihedral group with cyclic subgroup $C_n$, and let $W_l'$ be the subset arising at level $l$ in the three-reflection presentation construction used in the paper. Denote its stabilizer by

$$
\operatorname{Stab}(W_l')=\{c\in C_n:W_l'+c=W_l'\}.
$$

**Stabilizer conjecture.** The stabilizer of $W_l'$ is always either

$$
\{1\}\quad\text{or}\quad C_n.
$$

The conjecture is suggested by the proof of the preceding theorem, but the source gives no resolution or further context.
parsed.source_name: Michael Allocca and Max Trimmer, “Perturbation Effects on Word Lengths in Three-Reflection Symmetric Presentations of Dihedral Groups”, arXiv:2506.19216 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: The assignment-fixing conjecture for quadratic assignment solvers
parsed.statement: Let a quadratic assignment problem (QAP) instance be given, and suppose that a few assignments are identified as belonging to a high-quality solution. Consider permanently fixing those assignments and then solving the remaining problem. **Assignment-fixing conjecture.** If fixing these assignments and solving the remainder is a relatively effective strategy for the solver, then the max–min ant system (MMAS) will perform well relative to the breakout local search algorithm (BMA). The conjecture proposes a possible explanation for differences in algorithm performance across QAP instance classes, but the supplied text does not establish the effectiveness of the strategy or the predicted relative performance.
parsed.source_name: Jeffrey Christiansen and Kate Smith-Miles, “Instance Space Analysis for the Quadratic Assignment Problem”, arXiv:2506.20172 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20172

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

parsed.title: Conjecture on optimal independent spanning trees in random regular graphs
parsed.statement: Let $d=d(n)\in[3,n-1]$, and let $G\sim G(n,d)$ be a random $d$-regular graph. An **independent spanning tree** (IST) family is a collection of spanning trees whose root-to-vertex paths are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint. **Conjecture on optimal independent spanning trees in random regular graphs.** With high probability, $G$ contains $d$ ISTs if $d\neq n-3$, and contains $d-1$ ISTs if $d=n-3$. The paper identifies this as a strengthening of the sparse random-regular-graph question; the conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Lawrence Hollom, Lyuben Lichev, Adva Mond, Julien Portier and Yiting Wang, “Approximate Itai-Zehavi conjecture for random graphs”, arXiv:2506.23970 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23970

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2025). “He also proposed an analogue for directed graphs (Conjecture 6.7(a)), which was disproved by Huck .”

parsed.title: Hu–Ye multiplicity conjecture for hypermatrices
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be an order $h$ hypermatrix of dimension $n$, and let $\mu$ be an eigenvalue of $\mathcal{M}$. Write $am_{\mathcal{M}}(\mu)$ for its algebraic multiplicity and $gm_{\mathcal{M}}(\mu)$ for its geometric multiplicity. **Hu–Ye multiplicity conjecture.** One has

$$
am_{\mathcal{M}}(\mu) \geq gm_{\mathcal{M}}(\mu)(h-1)^{gm_{\mathcal{M}}(\mu)-1}.
$$

This conjecture relates algebraic and geometric multiplicities for eigenvalues of hypermatrices; the source gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Shashwath S Shetty and K Arathi Bhat, “Spectral Theory of Hypergraphs: A Survey”, arXiv:2507.13664 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13664

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

parsed.title: Palindromic complexity conjecture for languages with symmetric order conditions
parsed.statement: Let $L$) be a language on $k$ letters satisfying a symmetric order condition and having no connection. Its palindromic complexity is the number of palindromic factors of each length. **Palindromic complexity conjecture.** The palindromic complexity of $L$ is $1$ for even $n$ and $k$ for odd $n$. The conjecture is motivated by examples and by results suggesting that connections occurring in suitably paired bispecial factors do not reduce the number of palindromes; its general validity is not established in the source.
parsed.source_name: Sébastien Ferenczi and Luca Q. Zamboni, “Clustering, order conditions, and languages of interval exchanges”, arXiv:2507.17370 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17370

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

parsed.title: Monical–Tokcan–Yong's Bruhat-order polytope conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, and let $\leq_{S}$ be the Bruhat order on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ generated by the relations $\lambda>s_{ij}(\lambda)$ for $1\leq i<j\leq n$ and $\lambda_i<\lambda_j$, together with $s_{ij}(\lambda)>_{S}\lambda+e_i-e_j$ when $\lambda_j-\lambda_i>1$. Define

$$
\widehat{\mathcal{P}}_{\alpha}=\operatorname{conv}\{\gamma\in\mathbb{Z}^n:\gamma\leq_{S}\alpha\}.
$$

**Monical–Tokcan–Yong's conjecture.** If $\beta\in\widehat{\mathcal{P}}_{\alpha}$ and $\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^n_{\geq 0}$, then $\beta\leq_{S}\alpha$.

The paper states that its Theorem resolves this conjecture in the affirmative, so the claim is treated as solved.
parsed.source_name: Milo Bechtloff Weising and Alexander E. Black, “Saturation for Non-Symmetric Macdonald Polynomials”, arXiv:2508.00336 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00336

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed.title: The polytopal realization conjecture for ornamentation lattices
parsed.statement:
Let $D$ be a directed graph, and let $\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(D)$ denote its ornamentation lattice. **Polytopal realization conjecture.** For any directed graph $D$, the ornamentation lattice

$$
\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(D)
$$

is isomorphic to the transitive closure of the graph of a polytope oriented in a linear direction. This conjecture extends the corresponding result for unstarred increasing trees and answers a question posed for rooted trees; it remains open beyond the unstarred-tree case.
parsed.source_name: Antoine Abram, Jose Bastidas, Félix Gélinas, Vincent Pilaud and Andrew Sack, “Ornamentation lattices and intreeval hypergraphic lattices”, arXiv:2508.01606 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01606

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
